record_notes.DCP-LETT-1721: July 19, 1855 follows an earlier meeting, delayed by Hunt coal and iron inquiries. No surviving written Darwin prompt is identified. Hunt interprets Darwin aim as reproducing latitudinal solar conditions and proposes separate light, heat and actinism components, with explicit Norway/Italy/equator expressions. These are Hunt historical scientific claims. His pale blue, light yellow and red samples are for preliminary experiments; they are not yet identified with the intense book specifications. Physical glass enclosures are stated, not transcribed documents. Annotation marks are undated. Bibliography and later editorial explanation of Darwin aims remain separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1727: July 22 with supplied 1855 year directly thanks Hunt for both specimens and letter, matching 1721. Darwin finished the second edition of Researches on Light a few days earlier, not necessarily on receipt of the letter, and had independently decided to try three colours. He asks for a supplier and colouring materials, recognizing colour alone may not identify radiant properties. London visit on August 7–9 and showing glass samples are plans, not completed events. No exact physical receipt day or present purchase is asserted.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1730: July 24, 1855 answers the July 22 questions, a two-day composition interval. Hunt explicitly corrects Darwin: supplied samples are NOT the effective glasses described in Researches. He specifies fully tinted cobalt blue, silver yellow and copper red, names Bontemps at Chance Brothers, and permits use of his name. His absence prevents the proposed meeting, while museum forwarding remains possible. Footnote 1 mislabels the earlier July 19 letter as 1854; the actual source 1721 is July 19, 1855. Do not transfer this apparatus error into the chronology.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1734: July 31 with supplied 1855 year is a follow-up to Hunt supplier and colour advice, but its immediate difficulty comes from a missing enclosed manufacturer query. P2–6 reports acting on the exact three specifications and using Hunt name for plant experiments; that passage is supported by 1730. P1 asks about coated versus throughout-coloured glass and returning the enclosure, whose text, price and date are unavailable. Retain P1 as missing-input grounding rather than invent a Chance Brothers question. P7 is the closing. Purchase, delivery and successful experiments are not established.

reading_method: All four target bodies independently read in full with source headers, XML constraints, excluded salutations, annotations, footnotes and bibliography. No figures or unavailable body sources.
